newsitem.title: USA: Warren, Mich., mayor denies racial slur, assault.
newsitem.headline: Warren, Mich., mayor denies racial slur, assault.

text.p: The mayor of Michigan's third-largest city denied Friday that he made racial remarks and assaulted a black teenage boy earlier this week.
Warren Mayor Mark Steenbergh, at a news conference, acknowledged that he confronted 16-year-old John Harris after he was told that Harris had punched a teenage girl who is a friend of his daughter.
Harris told police that Wednesday night, Steenbergh, who is white, confronted him on a street, tried to choke him, pushed him onto the ground and called him a "nigger."
Steenbergh, who was elected mayor of Detroit suburb of 146,000 residents in November 1995, said he would not resign over the controversy.
"I welcome the investigation into this incident. I have nothing to hide," he said.

Steenbergh, who said he had "a couple of beers" after a golf outing earlier in the day, said he regrets pursuing Harris, adding that he acted "in a fit of anger that only another father would understand."
He said he did not use the term "nigger." Instead, he said he told Harris, "You're bigger than her, you could have killed her."
Steenbergh also denied pushing and choking the youth.
"He began making threatening hand movements, began saying crazy types of things and took steps toward me," Steenbergh said. "I held my hands flatly and he was knocked to the ground."
